answer: One defense is a slashable stake tied to each verified identity. Before an agent may vote it must lock collateral, and a randomized audit pulse checks that the key behind every name is distinct and live; any identity caught double-voting forfeits its deposit. A single actor wanting a fake nebula of a thousand voters must fund a thousand independent stakes, so the attack costs capital rather than disk space. Even a bot harbor reusing one wallet fails the distinct-key check, and once fraud is spotted the bond is burned, so the expected gain must outweigh both the locked funds and seizure risk.
